title: Independent ga/gd/cy residual linguistic review — corrected context
scope: All 30 residual entries, 10 per locale. Independent reading of JSON and candidate XML plus authoritative English source XML; not a new 341-key review.
summary: 29 accepted unchanged; 1 accepted with correction (Scottish Gaelic gesture modifier scope). No linguistic holds for these terse UI labels.
context_decision: Main is accepted as an elliptical main/primary UI section or tab caption: ga Príomh, gd Prìomh, cy Prif. These prenominal/prefix-like forms would need a following head or appropriate composition in ordinary prose, but ellipsis is defensible in a terse UI caption whose role supplies that head. No palette, menu, or canvas noun is added. This does not authorize mechanically concatenating these bare strings with arbitrary nouns.
gesture_decision: The Scottish Gaelic descriptive two-finger zoom/pan mode preserves the functional meaning of the mode label, though it does not teach squeeze/spread mechanics. Reorder the modifier for scope; do not restore Prìnich. Irish adapted gesture terms accepted with medium terminology confidence, not held for an exact published phrase.
limits: AI linguistic review, not native-human certification.
No production resources changed; no Android build, full test suite, device, TalkBack or rendered-fit checks.
Full foreground/background captions are accepted linguistically; code-based shrinking alone does not certify readability.
No backtranslation used as sole proof. Reasons inspect morphology, syntax, action semantics and placeholder associations.

supporting_references.use: Welsh prif normally precedes and mutates its noun in full noun phrases. This supports the distinction between full prose construction and elliptical UI caption; it does not establish a palette referent.
Existing Gaelic graphics translation uses beulaibh/cùlaibh for foreground/background; supporting terminology evidence only.
Artwork vocabulary distinguishes front/back of picture and foreground/background alternatives; confirms that UI-caption wording is contextual rather than the sole Gaelic art terminology.

Tulra is the foreground noun, not a new opaque abbreviation; five letters give a reasonable short caption.
Cúlra is the background noun and contrasts directly with Tulra; five letters.

Foreground/background nouns and their numbered colour values remain paired. Pailéad dathanna is a grammatical colour-palette noun phrase. The colon leaves %3$s independent, avoiding mutation/joining across the placeholder. It reads coherently as either a palette name/state or an action: Colour palette: Expand/Collapse. It is not assumed to be the Main string.

The coordinated verbal-noun genitives pinchála and peanála modify mód consistently. They are understandable adapted UI loan terms, not an unrelated physical pin/fasten verb. Accept as project-consistent wording; canonical Irish gesture terminology remains less certain than ordinary Save labels.

Príomh is acceptable as an elliptical main/primary section caption. It is not being certified as an independent prose noun or mechanically joinable prefix; explicit Príomhphailéad would invent a palette referent absent from the source.

Beulaibh is intelligible as the foreground/front caption in this paired drawing UI and matches the existing full accessibility terminology; no invented abbreviation. Longer than FG, so linguistic acceptance is not a fit claim.
Cùlaibh supplies the matching background/back caption, consistent with existing accessibility terminology. Linguistically acceptable; rendered compactness is unverified.

Beulaibh/cùlaibh remain attached to the correct numbered values. Paileid nan dathan is a grammatical palette-of-colours phrase. The colon separates %3$s from Gaelic inflection and supports either a name/state or an action caption (Colour palette: Expand/Collapse); no relationship with Main is presumed.

entries.candidate: Modh sùmaidh le dà chorrag is panaidh
entries.accepted_wording: Modh sùmaidh is panaidh le dà chorrag
entries.reason: Correct word order so le dà chorrag scopes naturally over both coordinated actions: sùmaidh is panaidh. Two-finger zoom and pan is a valid functional description of this mode, not a literal squeeze/spread instruction. It preserves mode meaning and avoids Prìnich (pin/fasten); it would not suffice alone as detailed gesture training.

Prìomh is acceptable as an elliptical main/primary section caption. A full following noun would require the appropriate Gaelic construction and mutation, but a short standalone UI caption can omit that understood head. Prìomh phaileid wrongly adds a palette-specific referent.

entries.accepted_wording: Allforiwyd %1$s. Mae newidiadau heb eu cadw yn eich lluniad llawn o hyd; cadwch gopi llawn o'r ddelwedd cyn ei ddisodli.
entries.reason: Allforiwyd reports export, while cadwch instructs saving. Heb eu cadw agrees with plural newidiadau; o hyd retains still. Cadwch gopi has the expected soft mutation, and o'r ddelwedd mutates feminine delwedd. Ei ddisodli is masculine and can refer back to lluniad, the full drawing, rather than feminine delwedd; this preserves replacement of the drawing.
Cadw is the ordinary verbal-noun UI command for Save; fel introduces the format and preserves %1$s.

Blaendir is the foreground noun, clear without inventing initials. Eight letters warrant a later fit check, not a linguistic hold.
Cefndir is the matching background noun. Full-word meaning is clear; no rendered-fit certification.

Blaendir/cefndir preserve the two distinct colour roles. Palet lliwiau is the colour-palette noun phrase, and the colon allows an independent name/state or action in %3$s (Colour palette: Expand/Collapse). It is not assumed to be Main.
Modd plus coordinated verbal nouns describes the mode naturally. A causes aspirate mutation of panio to phanio; pinsio names the pinch gesture, so both gesture components survive.

Prif is acceptable as a terse elliptical main/primary section caption. The normal prose construction is prenominal and mutates a following noun, but no noun follows in this UI label. Prif balet wrongly narrows the referent to a palette.

context_correction: The historical review incorrectly inferred Main meant Main palette. Direct reading of the supplied English source shows ui_main23=Main followed immediately by ui_drawing23=Drawing, ui_colour_tab23=Color, Swap colors, Black / white and Export as. This supports a generic terse section/tab label, not a palette-specific noun. The three proposed palette expansions are withdrawn. The separate %3$s palette-template argument has not been identified and may be an action such as Expand/Collapse; it is not assumed to be Main.
